name: STAGE
tagline: Streaming platform for films and shows in Indian dialects
excerpt: STAGE, an OTT app for Indian dialect content such as Haryanvi, raised a mix of equity and debt from three sharks in Shark Tank India Season 2.
content:
STAGE is a subscription streaming app built around regional dialects, starting with Haryanvi films, series and music. Its founders, Vinay Singhal, Parveen Singhal and Shashank Vaishnav, previously built the content site WittyFeed.

On Shark Tank India Season 2, Episode 3, the founders asked for ₹3 crore for 1%. They left with ₹3 crore in equity and debt at a ₹250 crore valuation from Namita Thapar, Aman Gupta and Peyush Bansal, according to Business Today. Half of the money, ₹1.5 crore, was debt, which Business Today later reported carried 18% interest, the highest rate offered that season.

Since the show, STAGE's filings show fast growth. Entrackr reported revenue from operations of ₹111 crore for FY25, based on documents filed with the Registrar of Companies, up from ₹18 crore a year earlier, while losses also grew. Inc42 reported in December 2024 that the company was raising ₹84.61 crore in Series B shares, led by Goodwater Capital and Blume Ventures.

The pitch is a reminder that a high asking valuation can still close when part of the cheque is structured as debt.

deal.terms: Plus ₹1.5 crore debt; Business Today reported the interest rate as 18%

faq.q: Did STAGE get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: Yes. Namita Thapar, Aman Gupta and Peyush Bansal put in ₹3 crore split between equity and debt, at a ₹250 crore valuation.
Entrackr reported revenue from operations of ₹111 crore for FY25, based on Registrar of Companies filings.
Yes. Its FY25 filings were reported in February 2026, and it raised a Series B round in 2024–25.
Vinay Singhal, Parveen Singhal and Shashank Vaishnav.

lessons: A debt component let the sharks accept a valuation close to the founders' ask while limiting their equity risk.
A defined niche (dialect content) gave the founders a clear answer to competition from large OTT platforms.
Growth since the show came with rising losses, which shows that a funded content business still burns cash on production.
notes: Equity/debt split: Business Today reports ₹3 cr total at ₹250 cr valuation and a ₹1.5 cr debt component, so equity is ₹1.5 cr = 0.6% (arithmetic). Interest rate conflict: Business Today 18%, Wikipedia 12%; we show Business Today's figure. Episode 3 confirmed by SET India official episode upload description.
